subject: Inference sprint — summary & proposed commitments
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ellis <sam@helionworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Inference sprint — summary & proposed commitments

Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap below so we have aligned next steps and ownership. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Intermittent 99th-percentile latency spikes impacting interactive search (visible during batch indexing windows).
- Throughput variability during peak business hours (need predictable tail latencies for SLAs).
- Concerned about model size & cost tradeoffs — want to balance quality for 512-token prompts with cost target ~ $0.0008/token.

SLO targets you called out:
- P99 latency: <= 300ms for prompt lengths up to 512 tokens (90% of traffic is sub-256).
- Steady-state throughput: 1,200 reqs/min with burst to 3k for 5–10 minute periods.
- Availability goal: 99.9% regional uptime; prefer compute in EU (primary) with US failover.

Model and deployment notes from the call:
- Primary model family: open-weights Llama-variant (quantized 4-bit/8-bit experiments).
- Candidate sizes: 13B (low cost), 33B (mid), 70B (high quality); you want a recommendation for the best cost/quality frontier.
- KV cache/ prefix caching expected to reduce repeat-token load for common session flows.

Proposed technical commitments (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Run a scoped load test using your representative prompt set (you to provide sample traces) — cadence: within 5 business days. Owner: Grace. Attachment: inference_slo_table.xlsx (initial SLO mapping).
2) Rack topology recommendation: Dedicated EU pool + autoscale tier + cross-region fallback. Include KV cache layer and prefix caching with 30s TTL for session traffic. Owner: Karthik.
3) Cost/quality report with model/quantization suggestions and expected per-token economics for your workload. Owner: Monica.
4) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and timeline (including security questionnaire handoff). Owner: Grace & CS.

Next steps I propose this week:
- Sam: send the sample traces and a short list of 10 representative prompts (attach as NDJSON).
- Redwood: we run a 2-hour load run and return a short report + adjusted SLO table.
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive to finalize topology and rollout plan (suggestion: Wed 10/28 or Thu 10/29).

Attachments: inference_slo_table.xlsx (initial SLO mapping)

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Hi Grace — thanks for the crisp recap, this matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We're EU-first for production; US region only as disaster-recovery/fallback.
- The 3k burst estimate corresponds to nightly indexing completion windows (usually 02:00–02:15 UTC).
- We'll attach sample_trace.ndjson and a short prompt set today.

I'm looping infra@helionworks.com on the trace/attachments so you have raw logs for the run. We'll aim to meet your 5 business day window for the initial load run.

Also happy to confirm Wed 10/28 10:00am CET for the technical deep-dive — Monica, Karthik, does that work on your side?

Thanks,
Sam

- Monica: owner for model quality/cost analysis. Please prepare a short table showing expected latency/throughput tradeoffs for 13B/33B/70B with Q4 and Q5 quant profiles.
- Mina: will you own the MAP/Metrics dashboard (SLO tracking) and the security handoff? We should also add an early risk item for SOC2 evidence any delivery depends on.

I've attached the initial SLO mapping (inference_slo_table.xlsx) and will drop the sample traces from Helion in the shared drive when Sam sends them.

On schedule: confirm availability for Wed 10/28 10:00am CET for the deep-dive. If that works, I'll send calendar invites and a short agenda (load test results, topology recommendation, MAP review).

—
Grace
